classification.difficultyReason: Identify each horizontal or vertical scale factor, rearranging the equations in c(i) and d(i), then map the supplied graph's key points and read the resulting intercepts. These are direct applications of taught dilation rules to unfamiliar curves, with all required graph features supplied.

content.prompt: In each case an unknown function has been drawn. Use dilations to draw the new functions indicated beneath each, then write down the $y$-intercept and zeroes of the dilated function.

spec.description: Unknown cubic-shaped curve reconstructed through the source zeroes and stationary points; no polynomial rule is asserted.

answer.worked: Halve each horizontal coordinate: $(x,y)\mapsto(\frac{x}{2},y)$. The stationary points become $(-\frac12,1)$ and $(\frac12,-1)$. The zeroes $-2,0,2$ become $-1,0,1$; the $y$-intercept remains $0$.

spec.description: Source curve horizontally compressed by one half; turning-point guides retained.

answer.worked: Double each vertical coordinate: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,2y)$. The stationary points become $(-1,2)$ and $(1,-2)$. Points on the $x$-axis stay on it, so the zeroes remain $-2,0,2$. The $y$-intercept remains $0$.

spec.description: Source curve vertically stretched by two, with stationary-point guides.
Unknown curve with two local minima and a central local maximum; source coordinate guides retained.
spec.mathematics: Touches at (−2,0); passes through (−1,1),(0,2),(1,1),(2,2). No formula inferred.

answer.worked: Double each horizontal coordinate: $(x,y)\mapsto(2x,y)$. The marked points become $(-4,0)$, $(-2,1)$, $(0,2)$, $(2,1)$ and $(4,2)$. Thus the $y$-intercept remains $2$ and the only zero is $x=-4$.

spec.description: Source curve stretched horizontally by two; all source coordinate guides transformed.

answer.worked: Halve each vertical coordinate: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,\frac{y}{2})$. The marked points become $(-2,0)$, $(-1,\frac12)$, $(0,1)$, $(1,\frac12)$ and $(2,1)$. The $y$-intercept is $1$ and the zero remains $x=-2$.

spec.description: Source curve compressed vertically by one half, with source guide lines.
spec.mathematics: Zero −2; local maximum (0,1); local minimum (1,1/2); point (2,1).

spec.description: Straight left branch joined to a curved right branch; dashed guides through (2,1).
spec.mathematics: Source points (−1,0),(0,1),(1,0),(2,1). No rule for the unknown function is asserted.

answer.worked: $\frac y2=h(x)$ is $y=2h(x)$, so double each ordinate. The points $(0,1)$ and $(2,1)$ become $(0,2)$ and $(2,2)$. The zeroes remain $x=-1,1$.

spec.description: Source piecewise curve vertically stretched by two.

answer.worked: Double each horizontal coordinate. The zeroes $-1,1$ become $-2,2$, and $(2,1)$ becomes $(4,1)$. The point $(0,1)$ stays fixed, so the $y$-intercept remains $1$.

spec.description: Source piecewise curve horizontally stretched by two.
Upper semicircle between −1 and 1 with upward outer rays.
spec.mathematics: Arc through (−1,0),(0,1),(1,0); rays extend upward and outward.

answer.worked: $2y=g(x)$ is $y=\frac12g(x)$, so halve every ordinate. The top of the arc moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,\frac12)$; the zeroes remain $x=-1,1$. The outer rays are also compressed vertically.

spec.description: Half-height upper elliptical arc and shallower outer rays.

answer.worked: Halve every horizontal coordinate. The arc endpoints become $(-\frac12,0)$ and $(\frac12,0)$, while $(0,1)$ stays fixed. The outer-ray points $(-2,1)$ and $(2,1)$ become $(-1,1)$ and $(1,1)$.
